rules.title: Anti-retaliation protection for tenants (reprisal presumption)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not threaten or take reprisals against tenants for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations, complaining to the landlord in writing, or joining a tenants' union. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed retaliatory unless the landlord rebuts it by clear and convincing evidence.
rules.key_value: 6-month rebuttable presumption; damages 1-3 months' rent or actual damages, whichever greater
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants of residential premises in Massachusetts who engaged in protected activity, such as enforcing housing laws, reporting violations, written complaints to the landlord, or tenants' union organizing. Lease waivers are void.
rules.exemptions: The presumption does not apply to termination notices for nonpayment of rent.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the tenant (or someone on the tenant's behalf) engaged in protected activity within the prior six months

rules.penalty: Damages of not less than one month's rent or more than three months' rent, or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus costs of suit and reasonable attorney's fee
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.
rules.conflict_note: This is an anti-retaliation rule, not a general just-cause eviction requirement. It is mapped to just_cause_eviction as the closest category. It also affects rent increases given within the six-month window. The document does not state an effective date.
